deviations.text: Appendix A says parameters are updated and that further knobs follow MedAlpaca defaults. Those defaults set use_lora true (r=8, alpha=16, dropout=0.1, q_proj and v_proj). finetune.sh overrides that to a full fine-tune of llama-13b-bf. This lock follows the 7B appendix cell (3 epochs) and the MedAlpaca LoRA defaults, not finetune.sh.
MedAlpaca train.py defaults train_in_8bit to true. This lock uses fp16, the same dtype as the locked zero-shot anchor on the A6000.

MedAlpaca's default model_max_length is 256. The longest PMData stress example in the released train pool is 1416 characters, so 256 tokens would cut off the sensor text. 2048 is the LLaMA context the MedAlpaca trainer itself names as the ceiling.
Effective batch stays 128 (paper batch size) via gradient accumulation. Per-device batch is 1 so one 48 GB GPU can hold fp16 7B at length 2048. MedAlpaca's per-device default is 2.

The paper's warmup is 100 steps on the merged, oversampled multi-dataset run. This cell trains on the PMData stress complement only (653 rows). At batch 128 that is about 16 optimizer steps, so warmup 100 would never reach the stated learning rate. Warmup is 0 here.
Appendix A oversamples and merges datasets for the multi-task fine-tune. It does not publish the oversampling rule for the single-dataset Table 4 cell. This lock does not oversample.
MedAlpaca train.py defaults val_set_size to 0.1 and would hold out part of the train pool. The only eval is the locked 299-item split, so val_set_size is 0.
Appendix A says sampling decode. The locked anchor scorer is greedy first-number MAE (do_sample false, max_new_tokens 120). Eval uses that scorer. It is not retuned.

Train rows are PMData_stress_train_all.json minus any sensor text that also appears in the locked 299-item eval (sha256 fea3b879…). The released pool has one such overlap; it is dropped. Their paper describes a 10% test split. We do not claim this eval is that split. Scoring the locked eval makes the fine-tune MAE comparable to our zero-shot 2.689.
